analysis:
Both supplied units are BASE text of docs/reference/configuration.md, lines 1-519. The only change is a docs-only insertion at head lines 587-596, a new "Prompt preparation and admission" section. Its patch excerpt is truncated mid-row and the head text is not supplied, so I could not see the final row (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE) or the implementation.

The documented controls add a prompt token-ID cache (PromptTokenCache.swift). It reuses token IDs of rendered chat-template pieces "already seen in the request's prefix-cache scope". Other documented properties:
- A background verification re-tokenizes samples and disables reuse on a mismatch or throw.
- The cache can be turned off, and the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE disable also turns it off.
- The capacity is 32 MiB LRU per tokenizer, with a 4096 MiB maximum.
- The template-loop rewrites (ChatTemplateLoopRewrites) are guarded by a load-time comparison.

The cache is described as per-tokenizer, in-memory and keyed to the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scope. That is consistent with the T-041 mitigation that cross-account entries cannot resolve. No at-rest artifact is described and there is no attestation or authorization change. I identified no concrete regression from the documentation.

Open questions for deeper review are in the code, which is not in this batch:
1. Whether PromptTokenCache keys on the same authenticated cacheSalt scope. A cross-scope hit would add a new same-or-cross-tenant TTFT timing oracle related to T-041/SEC-035 (A-001), and the timing oracle would then also cover the prompt-prep stage.
2. Whether cached pieces are wiped on unload, or tied to tokenizer lifetime in line with T-028.
3. Whether the 4096 MiB cap allows memory exhaustion for a malicious consumer (T-029 availability).

The T-041 threat model likely needs a note on this in-memory prompt-piece cache and its timing channel. That is a threat-model gap rather than a documentation defect, and it cannot be confirmed without the implementation.
